chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who found an animal that had been stolen from a neighbor of his, so he took it in order to bring it back to him, but it died. He said: “There is nothing upon him.”

key_terms.دَابَّةً: an animal or beast of transport/property
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: there is no liability upon him
key_terms.لِيَأْتِيَهُ بِهَا: in order to bring it back to him

ai.seo_question: Is a person liable if a stolen animal dies while he is returning it to its owner?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person who takes possession of a stolen animal only to return it to its owner. If the animal dies in that process, he bears no liability, indicating that one acting to restore another's property without wrongdoing is not held responsible.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3541 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Abu Abdullah (as).

He said: I asked him about a man who found a stolen animal that belonged to his neighbor, so he took it to return it to him, but the animal died.
Imam (as) said: "There is nothing (no liability) upon him."
